title: Amending Spark's Artifact requires holding 1% of SPK supply plus a published risk analysis
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1 opens the Root Edit process with a submission gate: a SPK token holder submits a draft Artifact Edit Proposal through the Powerhouse system, "must hold at least 1% of the total token supply to submit a proposal," and must also post it on the Sky Forum under the "Spark Prime" category.

Two different filters are stacked. The stake threshold is an economic filter against spam and against proposals from actors with no exposure to the consequences. The content requirement is a quality filter: the proposal "must include an upfront review of opportunities and associated risks, outlining expected benefits, potential risks, and corresponding mitigation strategies for consideration by the community."

The second filter is the more unusual one. Most token-governance systems accept any well-formed proposal and leave risk assessment to voters and commentators. Here the burden of articulating the downside is placed on the proposer as an admissibility condition, before any reviewer or voter engages.

The trade-off is access. At 1% of a 10-billion supply, the right to initiate change is confined to large holders and to the Nested Contributors who are explicitly exempted — deliberately trading breadth of participation for seriousness of proposals.
description: Root Edit proposals are gated by both a stake threshold and a content requirement: benefits, risks and mitigation strategies must be laid out for the community upfront.
